comment: Every entry point under scripts/e2e/, in one of two lists, read by .github/workflows/e2e.yaml.
`hosted` is the set a GitHub-hosted runner can run: each row says what the job must give that
script, and `why_hosted` is a note on why a hosted runner can run it, read by no job. `elsewhere`
is every other script, each with the `needs` its own header states; e2e.yaml refuses one by
name with that text, and the refusal is a failed job. Both lists together must name every
scripts/e2e/*.sh of the tree, and e2e.yaml's select job fails when one is missing or extra.
`apt` is what the job installs for that script alone, `bun` whether it needs bun and this
repository's node_modules, `evidence_variable` the environment variable the script reads for
its evidence directory (empty where it takes none and keeps its work directory instead), and
`timeout_minutes` the job's limit, measured from the script's header with headroom.

hosted.why_hosted: Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go and awk, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/child-adoption.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and this script starts none

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go and awk, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/ci-red-no-takeover.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and the script starts no container, installing the nats-server it needs with go install
DATABASE_URL is required and must name a loopback host; its prerequisite loop takes go, bun, curl, psql and openssl, and it starts no container

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go, bun (after bun install) and awk, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/handoff-records.sh; CI's pgvector service is the server it needs, its role creates Dispatch's database there, it builds and starts Dispatch and the daemon itself, and it reaches no outside service; a run takes two to four minutes
Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go and awk, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/merged-root-waits.sh; CI's service satisfies it, and this script starts none

Run it from a checkout on a Linux host with go and awk, as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=... bash scripts/e2e/no-required-checks.sh; the proof waits for three reads of what each base requires, so a run takes about seven minutes

The daemon refuses to start without tmux on PATH, and CI's tmux is the runner's apt binary; with LEGION_E2E_PG_DSN set the script starts no container of its own, which is how ci.yaml's test job already runs it

elsewhere.needs: a throwaway kind cluster with gVisor on an amd64 Linux host, with docker, go, kubectl, curl, zstd, a tar that supports --zstd and kind, and a worker image by digest (LEGION_E2E_IMAGE)
a real cluster (LEGION_E2E_RUNTIME_CONTEXT and a worker image by digest), a devbox daemon, a real Claude Code and Oh My Pi on a model route, and the smoke repository
a devbox: tmux, a real Claude Code and Oh My Pi on a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE, with a gateway or a key file), and the smoke repository
a devbox: tmux, the pinned Oh My Pi through mise, and its own Postgres and NATS containers, which it fetches from a registry outside this repository's own package (sjawhar/legion#2512)
a throwaway kind cluster with gVisor on an amd64 Linux host, with docker, go, kubectl, curl, zstd, a tar that supports --zstd and kind, and a worker image by digest (LEGION_E2E_IMAGE)

a model provider key of its own for each of its two models, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY, which this repository holds as no secret and will not: Sami answered that no API key goes into sjawhar/legion, and that a smoke test which calls a model runs in the deployment repository on workload identity federation (sjawhar/legion#2512)
a devbox: tmux, the pinned Oh My Pi on a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE), a Chromium that Playwright drives, and its own Postgres and NATS containers

an issue pod and a model provider, so it is run by hand and never in CI: a loopback Postgres with pgvector (LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN), the model gateway key file (/var/run/model-gateway-key/key, or SESSION_DELIVERY_MODEL_KEY_FILE), go, bun and the checkout's node_modules, jq, curl, socat 1.8.0 or later, setsid, psql, git, tar, pgrep, mkfifo and python3

gh acting as an App installed on sjawhar/legion-smoke with contents and pull-request write (the implement App), and jq; it pushes branches and opens pull requests there and waits on that repository's Actions queue
a live multi-repository run on the production cluster: it is the operator's acceptance observer, reads that run's daemon, Dispatch, GitHub and kubectl, and starts nothing of its own

a throwaway kind cluster with gVisor on an amd64 Linux host, an NFS server in that cluster, with docker, go, kubectl, curl, zstd, a tar that supports --zstd and kind, and a worker image by digest (LEGION_E2E_IMAGE)
a devbox: tmux, a real Oh My Pi on a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE), docker, and the secret store's GEMINI_API_KEY_TESTS

a devbox, run from the operator's own Oh My Pi session: LEGION_E2E_MODEL_GATEWAY_URL, SMOKE_UPSTREAM_NATS, a running Postgres container (ACCEPT_PG_CONTAINER, ACCEPT_PG_PORT), a nats-server (ACCEPT_NATS_BIN), and the proof human's gh
a devbox, run from the operator's own Oh My Pi session: a model route (LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE), SMOKE_UPSTREAM_NATS, Legion's two role Apps, and the proof human's gh
a real cluster from the devbox: LEGION_E2E_PLATFORM, LEGION_E2E_POD_REACHABILITY and LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ROUTE, the daemon's restricted identity, and a worker image by digest
the production cluster from the devbox, against production Dispatch, the production Envoy listener and production NATS, with real agents in the smoke repository
a projected service-account token the staging EKS cluster minted, and its own Postgres and NATS containers
